chunks: Ḥanān ibn Sadīr asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.

About the fasting person immersing himself in water, he said: “There is no harm, but he should not submerge himself; and a woman should not immerse herself in water, because she carries the water by her private part.”

key_terms.الصَّائِمِ: the person who is observing the fast
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water, the medium discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman, for whom a distinct ruling is stated
key_terms.بِقُبُلِهَا: by her private part; indicating the reason mentioned in the text
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is not objectionable in itself
key_terms.يَسْتَنْقِعُ: to immerse oneself or sit in water

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a fasting person immersing in water?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning immersion in water while fasting. It permits a fasting man to enter water with a restriction, and it separately forbids a woman from immersing herself due to the possibility of water entering through her private part.
